references.text: Prohibition against offering animals with defects to the Lord, which is an abomination - showing the seriousness of breaking the covenant
The law concerning what is devoted (cherem) - everything devoted to the Lord belongs to him and cannot be redeemed
The command to burn what is devoted with fire and not to covet silver or gold from it
Joshua's command that everything in Jericho should be devoted, and the warning against taking anything of what was devoted
The introduction to this event - Achan's faithlessness regarding the devoted things
Achan's confession where he admits that he saw, coveted, took, and hid what was devoted
Reference back to Achan's sin with the devoted things and how the whole community was affected
Like Adam they broke the covenant and were unfaithful to the Lord - the same theme of covenant breaking
Moses' prophecy that Israel would break the covenant and turn to other gods
The Lord's accusation against Israel for having broken the covenant which he had commanded their fathers
